_note: The ONE table behind every implementation of the artifact-root rule. Two exist — bin/lib/artifact-root.js (ships, used by migrate-artifacts) and test/artifact_root.py (used by the validator) — and test/artifact_root_test.py runs BOTH against this table and requires identical answers. A third implementation joins by passing the same table. This is the mechanism that keeps one rule from having two behaviours; a table per implementation would be two homes for one fact.
_markers: A directory is adopted as an artifact root only when it CARRIES a register. Bare existence is not enough: a project may keep an unrelated docs/evidence/, and adopting it would write a run's paperwork into somebody else's folder. Standing instruction #1 — assert the input is what you think before deciding on it.

cases.name: legacy-only
cases.why: the upgrade must be a no-op for every project already running: the old root exists, so it stays the root and nothing moves

cases.name: new-only
cases.why: a project that has migrated, or was seeded after the rename

cases.name: both-roots
cases.why: a partial migration is a legitimate state — the operator moves what they need and leaves the rest. The new root wins and the remainder is REPORTED rather than silently ignored

cases.name: fresh-project
cases.why: nothing exists yet: the default is the new name, which is how the rename reaches new projects without touching old ones

cases.name: configured-wins-over-legacy
cases.why: references/artifacts.md promised since v0.1.0 that a host project may relocate the root. Until now nothing kept that promise; paths.artifacts does, and it outranks both discovered names. The legacy directory is still reported as a leftover: `leftover` answers 'what else carries records here', which is a different question from 'which root won' and has the same answer however the root was chosen

cases.name: unrelated-new-dir-is-not-adopted
cases.why: a docs/evidence/ holding somebody else's material carries no register, so it is not a pipeline root and the legacy one still is. Adopting on bare existence is how a run's paperwork lands in an unrelated folder

cases.name: default-path-occupied-reports-collision
cases.why: the sharp edge of the previous case: no legacy root exists, so the default applies — straight into a directory somebody else owns. The resolver still answers, and flags it, so the CALLER asks instead of writing blind. A resolver that returned a bare string could not express this at all
